authoredPrompt: This figure is a heavily labeled diagram of a hyperbola opening left and right, centered at the origin of a coordinate system with arrowhead-tipped axes marked x at the right and y at the top. Two dark blue branches sweep away from the horizontal axis, one on each side. A pair of orange dashed lines cross at the center and run diagonally to the corners of the drawing, each tagged by a leader arrow reading "Asymptote" at the lower left and lower right. A teal dashed rectangle is centered on the origin, its vertical sides passing through the turning points of the two branches and its horizontal sides passing through two points on the vertical axis, with its corners sitting on the orange diagonals. A short red segment along the horizontal axis joins the two turning points and is labeled "Transverse axis" by an arrow pointing down onto it; a light blue segment along the vertical axis joins the top and bottom of the rectangle and is labeled "Conjugate axis." Dark blue dots at the ends of the red segment are each labeled "Vertex," light blue dots at the ends of the vertical segment are each labeled "Co-vertex," teal dots farther out along the horizontal axis are each labeled "Focus," and an orange marker at the crossing point is labeled "Center." Assembling every named element on one curve shows how the rectangle and its extended diagonals govern the directions the branches approach.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for transverse axis length: the learner moves the vertices outward or inward, the red axis and hyperbola branches update, and a sets where each branch turns.
- Slider for conjugate axis length: the learner changes the rectangle height, the asymptote slopes and branch openings update, and b controls the guide rectangle that determines approach directions.
- Toggle between guide rectangle and final curve: the learner switches the dashed rectangle and asymptotes on and off, the branches remain in place, and the role of the construction guides in shaping the hyperbola becomes clear.
authoredContext:
As with the ellipse, every hyperbola has two axes of symmetry. The transverse axis is a line segment that passes through the center of the hyperbola and has vertices as its endpoints. The foci lie on the line that contains the transverse axis. The conjugate axis is perpendicular to the transverse axis and has the co-vertices as its endpoints. The center of a hyperbola is the midpoint of both the transverse and conjugate axes, where they intersect. Every hyperbola also has two asymptotes that pass through its center. As a hyperbola recedes from the center, its branches approach these asymptotes. The central rectangle of the hyperbola is centered at the origin with sides that pass through each vertex and co-vertex; it is a useful tool for graphing the hyperbola and its asymptotes. To sketch the asymptotes of the hyperbola, simply sketch and extend the diagonals of the central rectangle. See the figure.

Key features of the hyperbola

This diagram illustrates the various components of a hyperbola centered at the origin, including the vertices, co-vertices, foci, transverse axis, conjugate axis, asymptotes, and the rectangular box used to construct the asymptotes.

In this section, we will limit our discussion to hyperbolas that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane; the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. We will consider two cases: those that are centered at the origin, and those that are centered at a point other than the origin.
